# dsh-ofm-codearts-pin

Pins `dsh-our-free-model` (OFM) to **2.5.8** — the last release that still ships
Huawei Cloud's **Co

deArts** channel, and the one where that channel was fixed —
and heals the install back to it on **e

nnel, and the one where that channel was fixed —
and heals the install back to it on **every boot**.
> 中文说明见 README.zh-CN.md。
## Why this exists

OFM 2.5.9 deleted the Huawei Cloud channel outright. The channel pack stops
registering `["CODEARTS"

, "codearts"]`, the settings page loses the card, and the
account entry (`codearts-…` in `~/.dsh/cha

nnel-pack/state.json`) plus its
credential are left behind, unusable and unreachable. Nothing in 2.5

.9 can be
configured back into existence.
Version history matters here:
| Release | CodeArts channel | Works? |
| 2.5.6 | present | **No** — its request signature is rewritten by any plugin that patches global `f

etch` (billion-context, cost-meter), so upstream rejects it |
| 2.5.7 | present | Yes — PR #481 move

d CodeArts onto an independent signed transport and added the 4004 retry |
| **2.5.8** | **present**

| **Yes** — and it is the newest build that still has the channel |
| 2.5.9 | deleted | — |
So 2.5.8 is the correct landing point: newest, and working.
## What it does
| Step | Behaviour |
| Byte check | On each boot, all 80 installed files are compared to the shipped payload by SHA-256 |
| Exact repair | Only files whose hash actually differs are rewritten; each is backed up, replaced

atomically, read back and re-hashed |
| Syntax gate | Every `.js` it writes is `node --check`-ed; a

file that fails is restored from backup immediately |
| All-or-nothing | If any step in a pass fails
, every file that pass already wrote is rolled back — a half-applied pin never reaches the next boot

|
| Payload gate | The archive is unpacked and every extracted file re-hashed first; a payload that

fails verification aborts the pin without writing a byte |
| Update check | Sets `updateCheckHours

= 0` in `~/.dsh/our-free-model/settings.json` (OFM's own documented opt-out, one key only) |
| Hones
t report | `index.js`, `client.js` and `package.json` were already read by the time this plugin runs
, so the report says `restart required` rather than claiming the whole change is live |

The payload is not a rebuild. It is the exact file set that 2.5.8's own
**Ed25519-signed** `feed/man

ifest.json` pins, copied byte-for-byte — which is what
makes "restore" reproducible instead of a sna

pshot of whatever happened to be
installed.

It ships as `vendor/payload/2.5.8.tar.gz` (the same form upstream publishes),
unpacked on first use

to `~/.dsh/ofm-codearts-pin/payload-2.5.8/` and verified
file by file before anything is written. Th

e archive form exists because
upstream's `pack.js` embeds a Google OAuth client secret: loose files

make the
repository unpushable (GitHub push protection rejects the commit), and rewriting
that byte

would change the hash the pin is built on. The archive is the only
shape that is both byte-exact and

ge the hash the pin is built on. The archive is the only
shape that is both byte-exact and pushable.
## Install

Or from the tarball / git (all three `dsh.install` entries are filled in).

⚠️ **Order matters.** In `dsh.profile.bundles`, this plugin must appear **before**
`dsh-our-free-mod

el`. That way OFM has not yet imported
`vendor/channel-pack/pack.js` when the pin lands, so the heal

ed pack is the one
that loads and CodeArts is back on that same start. The row in
`cordis.patch.yml`

is an id-addressed insert: it adds itself, it does not move
OFM.

## The one thing it cannot do for you

The profile's **tarball specifier**. If `dependencies["dsh-our-free-model"]` still
points at an olde

r package, the next `pnpm install` reinstalls that build
underneath the pin. The status output shows

the specifier currently in use and
warns about it, but it does not edit profile dependencies — that

is the package
manager's territory. Point it at the 2.5.8 tarball.
## Tests

Two suites, both against throwaway fixtures in a temp directory — no network, no
touching a real ins

uites, both against throwaway fixtures in a temp directory — no network, no
touching a real install:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

Covered: the archive extracts exactly the 80 files the manifest pins; a corrupt
archive is refused;

a clean install is left untouched; a 2.5.9-shaped install is
healed (both channel halves return); a

single drifted file is the only one
written; a poisoned payload entry is refused; a mid-pass failure

rolls everything
back; backups and undo; stale staging files are swept; `quietUpdates` touches one

key; a foreign `.bak` is never mistaken for ours. `test:boot` additionally proves
`apply()` cannot t

hrow, that the command and read-only route each register once,
and that a re-apply is idempotent.

ayload, redistributed under that project's
MIT licence (see the last section of `LICENSE`). This plu

gin does not alter
upstream behaviour, branding or endpoints — it only restores files that belong to
